notation: concert pitch:quarter-note length; _:length is a rest; each string is a 4/4 bar

phrases.name: Sea-wall call
phrases.change: Triadic lift reaches a dominant answer; the final rest leaves the next launch clear.

phrases.name: Evacuation answer
phrases.change: The answering descent closes lower than the call and changes its final rhythm.

phrases.name: Above the sea wall
phrases.change: The opening cell fragments upward and reaches the first high E.

phrases.name: Corridor opens
phrases.change: Longer suspension and stepwise release relax the preceding ascent.

phrases.name: City in shadow
phrases.change: Relative-minor register drop and wider rests make space for the burning city.

phrases.name: Turning toward the line
phrases.change: The bass route leaves the minor center and the line earns a new F-sharp summit.

phrases.name: Rooftop crossings
phrases.change: Contrary registral motion turns repeated climbs into alternating rooftop arcs.

phrases.name: Break through the fire
phrases.change: The melodic sequence changes direction each bar and saves the highest G for the breach.

phrases.name: Saltlight return
phrases.change: The original head returns with a higher continuation and a suspended answer.

phrases.name: Course back to the coast
phrases.change: An unclosed dominant leaves a clear breath and points back to the opening D.

phrases.name: Warden intercept
phrases.change: The coastal triad compresses into a minor attack and displaced rests.

phrases.name: Broadside answer
phrases.change: The answer sustains the first beat, reverses the arpeggiated route and lands on the leading tone.

phrases.name: Blockade closes
phrases.change: Sequence rises across changing bass roots; the final bar tightens into the dominant.

phrases.name: Under the gun deck
phrases.change: A low, exposed version of the call clears space before the final assault.

phrases.name: Attack the command bridge
phrases.change: The triad now starts above the original range and climbs to the dominant seventh.

phrases.name: Frigate turns to fire
phrases.change: A shortened falling return retains the coastal identity while the dominant resets combat.

phrases.name: A signal in the ice
phrases.change: An isolated fifth leap is answered by a Dorian sixth and a falling third.

phrases.name: Crystal answer
phrases.change: The answer fills the original silence and reaches the Dorian color above the line.

phrases.name: Through blue fractures
phrases.change: The signal is rhythmically broadened, then moves down through a full register.

phrases.name: Suspended corridor
phrases.change: Prepared A falls to G while accompaniment clears its third; the cadence remains remote.

phrases.name: Relay refractions
phrases.change: Related rising cells gain different continuations and a new high E.

phrases.name: The moon remembers
phrases.change: The same signal now rises from below and opens into a major arrival.

phrases.name: Distant signal return
phrases.change: The signal head returns with a shorter gap, a new upper turn and an ascending answer.

phrases.name: Under the relay lights
phrases.change: A modal settling gesture leaves half a beat before the original isolated E.

phrases.name: RIME acquires the signal
phrases.change: The long-distance signal loses its sustain and becomes clipped tracking bursts.

phrases.name: Hunter arms answer
phrases.change: The reply changes the attack positions and drives toward a lower leading tone.

phrases.name: Frost breach
phrases.change: F-natural interrupts the Dorian memory and resolves into E before the dominant peak.

phrases.name: Cold central eye
phrases.change: A stripped signal reveals its original spacing but alters the suspended answer.

phrases.name: Pursuit vectors
phrases.change: The fleeting Dorian sixth now initiates a registral chase through different chord shapes.

phrases.name: The hunter re-locks
phrases.change: A changed signal head falls through the intrusive F harmony before resetting on B.

phrases.name: Command on an open channel
phrases.change: A clipped command pickup meets weighty quarter-note answers.

phrases.name: The squadron answers
phrases.change: The answer changes the harmonic route and sends the command below its starting register.

phrases.name: Shipyard gantries
phrases.change: Alternating downward and upward spans trace the gantries without copying the command period.

phrases.name: Drop into the trench
phrases.change: A low falling route narrows the space before an upward dominant signal.

phrases.name: Hold your breath
phrases.change: Long notes and low dominant support create a clearing inside the driving approach.

phrases.name: Weapon emplacements
phrases.change: The command fragments into escalating thirds; diminished pressure has a directed dominant release.

phrases.name: Asterion behind us
phrases.change: A major-side refuge broadens the melody before the carrier blocks the route.

phrases.name: Last light in the trench
phrases.change: A long rising chain saves the octave C for the approach climax.

phrases.name: Command returns changed
phrases.change: The command pickup is recognizable; its answer now rises and the cadence changes roots.

phrases.name: Commit to the core
phrases.change: A falling unclosed G dominant points back into the command pickup.

phrases.name: Sovereign fires
phrases.change: The command pickup becomes a clipped low attack and the answer loses its safe major refuge.

phrases.name: Carrier armor
phrases.change: Broad armor phrases alternate whole-register descent and ascent.

phrases.name: Jump-drive charge
phrases.change: Diminished thirds compress the march while a high leading tone points toward the core.

phrases.name: The command core is exposed
phrases.change: A bare low command and prepared fourth-to-third resolution reveal the core.

phrases.name: All weapons converge
phrases.change: The mission summit is re-earned through a compressed high command and contrary bass route.

phrases.name: Threshold pressure
phrases.change: The opening head returns with a changed climb, then descends into the loop dominant.

phrases.name: Jackal tread riff
phrases.change: A low blues pickup and semitone approach lock onto the tank backbeat.

phrases.name: Convoy answer
phrases.change: The answer begins on the bass pickup and redirects the riff into a brighter Dorian route.

phrases.name: Jets over the causeway
phrases.change: Wide leaps crest above the low riff for the jet-assisted jump.

phrases.name: Foundry rollers
phrases.change: The riff fragments through changing bass roots and alternates rising and falling machinery.

phrases.name: Empty broken span
phrases.change: The tread rhythm drops out, leaving low notes and open space over the causeway.

phrases.name: Furnace mouths
phrases.change: Minor subdominant heat replaces the Dorian lift and the chromatic pickup returns in descent.

phrases.name: Jackal finds a lane
phrases.change: A major-side opening becomes a Dorian climb, then settles in the original low register.

phrases.name: Steel under fire
phrases.change: Short anacruses climb to the strongest dominant color of the mission.

phrases.name: Treads catch again
phrases.change: The recognizable tread head gets a new upper answer, then falls beneath the convoy.

phrases.name: Toward the siege line
phrases.change: A shorter blues gesture drops to E, leaving room for the riff pickup at the loop.

phrases.name: Iron Maw footprint
phrases.change: The tread riff is augmented and interrupted by a flat-second footprint.

phrases.name: Crushing counterstroke
phrases.change: The answer alternates high and low weight, then climbs on the dominant seventh.

phrases.name: Piston tower
phrases.change: A rising piston sequence increases register without reusing the original riff rhythm.

phrases.name: Broken crawler armor
phrases.change: Low sustained roots and separated replies expose the machinery between attacks.

phrases.name: Siege retaliation
phrases.change: The tread returns as a climbing attack while the flat-second reply falls across the line.

phrases.name: Tracks close the circle
phrases.change: The original chromatic pickup now falls into the low dominant before the crawler advances again.

phrases.name: Dragonfly beacon
phrases.change: A broad rising third and falling fifth identify the carrier beacon over 3+3+2 phrasing.

phrases.name: The wide interception arc
phrases.change: An answering curve changes the chord route and ends with an ascending dominant arc.

phrases.name: Bombers beyond the ring
phrases.change: Shorter notes and relative-minor footing turn the broad beacon into a warning.

phrases.name: Hold the carrier line
phrases.change: Sustained upper notes give the defensive orbit a stable center.

phrases.name: Climbing turnaround
phrases.change: The beacon third expands into a full climbing turnaround before falling back toward the carrier.

phrases.name: Across the vulnerable side
phrases.change: A low arc and changing phrase endpoints make the patrol feel newly exposed.

phrases.name: Beacon in the clear
phrases.change: The beacon head returns with an added summit and a suspended, unresolved answer.

phrases.name: Keep the circle open
phrases.change: An open dominant rises toward the beacon B rather than stopping on a full cadence.

phrases.name: Harrow inverts the beacon
phrases.change: The beacon third turns downward, starts off the beat and falls through the carrier harmony.

phrases.name: Hunter crosses the wake
phrases.change: The reply trades a downbeat climb for an offbeat answer and a long falling dominant.

phrases.name: Narrowing defense ring
phrases.change: The broad orbit contracts into a compressed falling cell while the dominant climbs.

phrases.name: Dragonfly exposed
phrases.change: The wide original breathing briefly returns in a lower, vulnerable register.

phrases.name: Intercept from above
phrases.change: The carrier beacon fights back in a shorter high-register arc before the hunter dominant.

phrases.name: Blind arc reopens
phrases.change: The initial inversion now leaps upward before its changed descent resets the pursuit.

phrases.name: Lightning cuts the conduit
phrases.change: A sixteenth spark and a missing beat establish the storm cut; three-part accents follow.

phrases.name: Ride the clear interval
phrases.change: The answering line widens into longer arcs and replaces the opening harmonic route.

phrases.name: Storm-vane sequence
phrases.change: Fragmented sparks rise through a new bass route toward a dominant upper seventh.

phrases.name: Fall behind the lightning front
phrases.change: A descending contour mirrors the storm climb and opens a gap before the eye.

phrases.name: Eye of the storm
phrases.change: Long notes and reduced percussion leave an audible calm between lightning fronts.

phrases.name: Conduits reconnect
phrases.change: Short sparks rebuild the pulse but the continuation stays broader than the opening.

phrases.name: Light through the cloud deck
phrases.change: An A-major clearing removes the dominant and turns the line toward a broad minor landing.

phrases.name: Above the final front
phrases.change: The register peaks at high B, then collapses toward the exposed dominant root.

phrases.name: Lightning call returns
phrases.change: The spark head returns, but its destination, second-bar direction and dominant ending all change.

phrases.name: Bring the squadron home
phrases.change: A falling final arc leaves a quiet dominant breath for the next storm cut.

phrases.name: Crown claims the storm
phrases.change: The lightning spark becomes a four-note cut, interrupted by a deliberate flat-second front.

phrases.name: Fortress storm reply
phrases.change: The answer starts on a held peak and moves through changing registers rather than copying the cut.

phrases.name: Strip the storm vanes
phrases.change: A descending series of vane calls meets an ascending dominant counterforce.

phrases.name: Heart above the clouds
phrases.change: The cut expands into silence and a prepared B-to-A release reveals the fortress heart.

phrases.name: Crown unleashes the front
phrases.change: The original spark reaches its only high C-sharp while the flat second forces a new route.

phrases.name: Storm front closes again
phrases.change: The four-note cut returns as a falling line, then a flat-second detour redirects the loop dominant.

phrases.name: The ferry answers the flare
phrases.change: The coastal triadic head becomes a short flare, answered through a new dominant-first route.

phrases.name: Escort the first sector
phrases.change: The answer alternates short intercepts and longer downward reassurance.

phrases.name: Fire crosses the wake
phrases.change: Rising fragments make the escort urgent, then fall toward the ferry instead of closing.

phrases.name: Find the sheltered channel
phrases.change: The melody lowers its destination across four bars to make the approaching shelter audible.

phrases.name: Under the sea-wall shelter
phrases.change: A lower augmented coastal gesture removes the backbeat and leaves a sheltered breath.

phrases.name: Lanterns ready to depart
phrases.change: A suspended answer raises the ferry out of the respite before the next sector.

phrases.name: The second sector opens
phrases.change: The flare head now clears a higher destination, and its answer climbs instead of falling.

phrases.name: Cover the open water
phrases.change: Alternating cover arcs let the second sector develop independently of the first.

phrases.name: The far shore is in sight
phrases.change: The last rising flare earns one brief high G and then settles into a broader major answer.

phrases.name: Keep one light on the water
phrases.change: A changed low flare acknowledges the civilian landing while the open dominant preserves the gameplay loop.

phrases.name: Measure the courier signal
phrases.change: Aurora’s isolated fifth is subdivided into a measured targeting cell with a new Dorian endpoint.

phrases.name: Compute the crossing
phrases.change: Short launches change interval size and destination as the route crosses separate ice lanes.

phrases.name: Pursuit beneath the arches
phrases.change: The pursuit opens into longer high arcs and first exposes a functional B dominant.

phrases.name: The false departure lane
phrases.change: A low detour rebuilds the targeting cell before it re-enters the courier’s altitude.

phrases.name: Observe through the ice
phrases.change: The hunter briefly holds its calculation; the prepared fourth releases without erasing the distant signal.

phrases.name: High intercept window
phrases.change: The measured fifth leaps into a changed high landing and is answered by an ascending dominant.

phrases.name: Drive disabled
phrases.change: Descending targeting fragments lower the line as the courier stops rather than claiming a full victory cadence.

phrases.name: Secure the approach codes
phrases.change: A new A-major opening and one high B mark the completed intercept while pressure remains.

phrases.name: Signal returns with the codes
phrases.change: The exact fifth head returns with a shorter continuation, new harmonic route and rising answer.

phrases.name: Meridian homeward
phrases.change: A lower modal settling gesture leaves room for the opening measurement to start again.

phrases.name: Keep the gantry steady
phrases.change: The command pickup doubles its first duration and stays low while the structure is stabilized.

phrases.name: Balance the collapsing frame
phrases.change: The response alternates a supported upper hold with a low counterweight.

phrases.name: Emergency clamps hold
phrases.change: Separated notes and reduced density mark controlled progress without a triumphant close.

phrases.name: Walk the load across
phrases.change: The augmented command gains shorter replies as stabilization becomes more confident.

phrases.name: A clear evacuation signal
phrases.change: A restrained major-side clearing finishes the controlled emergency before the wreck shifts.

phrases.name: The yard begins to fall
phrases.change: The stable command breaks into a clipped pickup and a diminished rupture.

phrases.name: Choose the wreck corridor
phrases.change: An alternating high-and-low escape line reverses the stabilization contour.

phrases.name: Under the broken assembly
phrases.change: Escape fragments crest at a short B-flat and fall through the unstable command harmony.

phrases.name: The command finds an exit
phrases.change: The original command rhythm returns, with a new climbing answer aimed toward the exit.

phrases.name: Clear of the falling yard
phrases.change: The exit narrows to the low command register and leaves the emergency loop open.

phrases.name: Share the weather call
phrases.change: The storm spark broadens into a two-beat call; another flight answers in the spaces.

phrases.name: Rivals learn the same lane
phrases.change: The answer becomes the next call; natural sixths distinguish forecast hope from the original minor storm.

phrases.name: Forecast the first gap
phrases.change: A major-side clearing opens the shared route; one high B marks the forecast crest.

phrases.name: Storm hands across the wing
phrases.change: Borrowed minor-weather harmony tightens the shared call before the corridor opens.

phrases.name: The safe corridor is real
phrases.change: Long Dorian tones and a quiet foundation reveal an actual calm corridor.

phrases.name: Recover the other flight
phrases.change: A low rescue call is answered upward before both parts regain the corridor.

phrases.name: Intertwined climb
phrases.change: The flights exchange complete climbs instead of doubling the same high line.

phrases.name: Forecast the return crossing
phrases.change: A borrowed D front passes through E into a brighter B forecast; each voice keeps its own landing.

phrases.name: A shared call returns changed
phrases.change: The opening call gains a higher destination; its partner now answers downward through a different register.

phrases.name: Leave the corridor open
phrases.change: A final low answer leaves the dominant open and hands the next loop back to the shared call.
